title: de.hubtask.work.template.instantiated.v1
description: A template was stamped out: one call produced a tree of entries from a shape somebody had defined earlier (D-06). It is published beside the item.created of each entry rather than instead of them - what happened to the world is that entries came into being - and what it adds is which template they came from and how large the tree is, so that a consumer can decide whether to look before it reads a hundred creations one at a time. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: Which template, which root entry, where it landed, and how many entries came out. The count is the whole tree including its root, which is what makes it comparable with the number of item.created events that accompany it.

template_id.description: The template that was stamped out. It may since have been deleted - a template is soft-deleted and the trees it produced stand on their own.

root_item_id.description: The entry at the top of the tree that came out, and the event's subject.

collection_id.description: The collection the tree landed in, and the one an actor's permission to see it is judged against.

created.description: How many entries came out, the root included. At least 1 and at most the node cap a template may hold (500).
